title: CLI error `This: command not found`
impact: Anyone installing lightningcss-cli where dependency install scripts don't run: pnpm >= 10 by default (verified with 10.28.0), bun (untrusted lifecycle scripts blocked by default), npm/yarn with ignore-scripts. 3 reactions here, duplicate #1193 (pnpm, 1.32.0) with more reports; these package-manager defaults are spreading, so impact grows. CLI-only, which is less used than the npm API.
code: cli/lightningcss (placeholder text file used as the npm bin)
cli/postinstall.js (replaces it with the native binary from lightningcss-cli-<platform>)
summary: lightningcss-cli's bin is a text file ('This file is required so that npm creates the lightningcss binary on Windows.') which postinstall.js overwrites with a hard link or copy of the platform binary. When the postinstall script doesn't run, the shell executes the sentence and fails with `This: not found` (exit 127). Fix: make the bin a real `#!/usr/bin/env node` launcher that resolves `lightningcss-cli-<platform>` and spawns it (esbuild's pattern), and keep postinstall only as an optimization that swaps in the native binary.
repro: 757-repro.mjs runs `sh cli/lightningcss --version` from the checkout (identical to the published file): status=127, 'cli/lightningcss: 1: This: not found'. Real install: `pnpm add -D lightningcss-cli@1.33.0` with pnpm 10.28.0 prints 'Ignored build scripts: lightningcss-cli@1.33.0', then node_modules/.bin/lightningcss gives '... lightningcss: 1: This: not found', exit 127. Adding pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies: ['lightningcss-cli'] and reinstalling makes it work.
evidence: Ran the repro on local + 1.31.1..1.33.0 (all WRONG; the file hasn't changed since the #282 fix in 1.15). Installed lightningcss-cli@1.33.0 in a scratch dir with pnpm 10.28.0, with and without onlyBuiltDependencies.

fix.approach: Replace cli/lightningcss with a Node launcher (shebang, resolve lightningcss-cli-<triple>/lightningcss[.exe], spawnSync with stdio inherit, forward exit code), with a clear error naming the missing platform package. Keep postinstall to overwrite it with the native binary for speed. Check the Windows path (postinstall currently deletes `lightningcss` and relies on npm's cmd shim). A cheaper interim step: make the placeholder a shell script that prints 'postinstall did not run; allow build scripts for lightningcss-cli' and exits 1.

draftReply:
Thanks for the report. This happens when `lightningcss-cli`'s install script doesn't run. The package ships a placeholder `lightningcss` file, and a `postinstall` script replaces it with the native binary for your platform. pnpm 10+ and Bun skip dependency install scripts by default (as does npm with `ignore-scripts`), so the placeholder text stays and the shell tries to run it as a command.

I reproduced it with `pnpm add -D lightningcss-cli@1.33.0` on pnpm 10.28. Until this is fixed, you can allow the script to run:

- pnpm: run `pnpm approve-builds`, or add `"pnpm": {"onlyBuiltDependencies": ["lightningcss-cli"]}` to package.json and reinstall
- Bun: add `"trustedDependencies": ["lightningcss-cli"]` to package.json and reinstall

A fix that doesn't depend on install scripts would make the CLI work out of the box. #1193 has the same cause.
